messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected in inference-us-west-2 (model-runner). Trigger: runtime-crash >5% errors over 5m. Pager: @oncall-maya. Alert link: https://alerts.redwood.example/incidents/4377778000

oncall-maya: I'm on it. Pulling up dashboards and recent deploys now.

eng-julian: seeing repeated segfaults in the model runner logs, probable native crash inside quant kernel. grabbing stacktrace...

eng-julian: ```
Thread 0 Crashed:
 0  libquant.so     0x7f1a2c3e attention_qk.cu + 0x14b
 1  libruntime.so   0x7f1a1a9f model_step + 0x2f3
 2  rwd_infer       0x55aa12 invoke_layer + 0x7b
```

sre-luke: can you confirm which model variant is affected? hosted vs dedicated?

eng-julian: initial look: affected pool = hosted-gpu-pool-3, model = summarization-xlarge-quant (deploy 1.13.0-quant). Dedicated customers unaffected so far.

customer-success-amy: we already have 3 customer tickets (CS-894, CS-896, CS-899) reporting 502s for summarization API. Logged in case of priority escalation. Sending an update to customers now.

oncall-maya: mitigation plan: 1) route production traffic for summarization-xlarge to fallback model `summarystable-v1` 2) scale up fallback pool 3) drain affected nodes and collect core dumps 4) rollback quant runtime to 1.12.3 if needed. Starting (1) now.

ops-bot: Executing runbook step: applying routing override -> `route-override set summarization-xlarge -> summarystable-v1` (operator: oncall-maya).

infra-bot: override applied. All new requests for summarization-xlarge routed to summarystable-v1 (warm instances scaled to 150%).

oncall-maya: traffic has been routed. Observability: error rate dropping from 6.1% -> 1.5% in the last 30s. Latency stable. :thumbsup:

eng-julian: starting node drain on hosted-gpu-pool-3 to get cores/logs: `rwdctl node drain hosted-gpu-pool-3-node-7 --reason "oom/segfault spike" --collect-cores`

eng-julian: found a repeating pattern in the runner log before crash: `kv_cache_size == 0` followed by `invalid pointer deref` in attention_qk. suspect pointer corruption after recent quant memory optimization.

sre-luke: what's customer impact (requests failed, percent of customers)?

customer-success-amy: CS update: 3 customers affected, ~1200 failed requests in last 10m, SLA page updated. Customers informed of failover to fallback model.

eng-julian: I'm initiating rollback of quant runtime on the affected pool to 1.12.3 now. Command: `deployment rollback summarization-xlarge --runtime-version 1.12.3 --pool hosted-gpu-pool-3`

ops-bot: Rollback started by eng-julian. Estimated completion ~3-5m.

oncall-maya: monitoring metrics — error rate is at 0.9% and decreasing, most traffic now on summarystable-v1. I'm going to hand off to eng-runtime for full postmortem and root cause analysis. I'm unpagable starting in 2h. @eng-julian @sre-luke please take over.

eng-julian: ack. Will collect cores, upload to S3, and start an issue with reproducer and regression test. Preliminary hypothesis: quant memory optimization introduced an unsafe pointer on long KV cache sequences.

sre-luke: creating incident doc and timeline. Will coordinate with CS for final customer messaging and remediation notes.

customer-success-amy: customers acknowledged update and appreciate the quick failover. Keeping tickets open until rollback confirmed and postmortem published.

eng-julian: rollback completed. Error rate back to baseline (<0.3%). Leaving fallback routing in place for 30m while we validate.

oncall-maya: thanks team. Move incident to monitoring -> postmortem. tagging incident: severity=high, cause=quant-runtime-crash (suspected).

infra-bot: Incident auto-note: cores collected -> s3://incidents/4377778000/cores/, logs -> s3://incidents/4377778000/logs/

eng-julian: next steps: reproduce locally with reproducer, add safety checks in KV cache codepath, and add scale-safe e2e tests for quantized runtime.

sre-luke: handing off final timeline and action items to eng-runtime. Closing active pager. :white_check_mark:
